Cells in this table containing data have been randomly adjusted to avoid the release of confidential data. Discrepancies may occur between sums of the component items and totals.
(a) See the methodology for definitions of sweetened beverages.
(b) Includes beverages reported as consumed on day prior to interview (Day 1).
(c) Sex recorded at birth refers to what was determined by sex characteristics observed at birth or infancy.

(d) A lower Index of Disadvantage quintile (e.g. the first quintile) indicates relatively greater disadvantage and a lack of advantage in general. A higher Index of Disadvantage (e.g. the fifth quintile) indicates a relative lack of disadvantage and greater advantage in general. See Socio-Economic Indexes for Areas (SEIFA), Australia, 2021 (abs.gov.au).
(e) Includes persons whose sex recorded at birth was another term (other than male or female).
(f) Includes sugar-sweetened commercial ice tea (eight digit food code: 11103001). See the AUSNUT 2023 food and dietary supplement classification for further information.

(g) Includes intense-sweetened commercial ice tea (eight digit food code: 11103003) and kombucha (eight digit food code: 11103004). See the AUSNUT 2023 food and dietary supplement classification for further information.
(h) Includes sugar- and intense-sweetened electrolyte drinks.
(i) Includes sugar- and intense-sweetened energy drinks.

(j) Includes fortified packaged water (five digit food code: 11803) and flavoured packaged water (five digit food code: 11804). See the AUSNUT 2023 food and dietary supplement classification for further information.
(k) Includes sugar- and intense-sweetened fruit and vegetable drinks.
(l) Includes aloe vera juice (eight digit food code: 11302001). See the AUSNUT 2023 food and dietary supplement classification for further information.
